key_findings: Rebellion acquired The Bitmap Brothers brand and entire portfolio in 2019, creating an unusually strong modern licensing route for Speedball, Xenon, The Chaos Engine, Gods and related titles.
Rebellion actively released a new Speedball in 2026, so Speedball is currently exploited IP rather than dormant abandonware.

Sensible Software's key rights route runs through Codemasters; Jon Hare has publicly described Sensible Soccer as owned by Codemasters, and current trademark evidence places SENSIBLE with Electronic Arts.
EA completed its acquisition of Codemasters in 2021; this creates a strong corporate/licensing route but does not eliminate release/component-level verification.
Football games require separate data/trademark/likeness analysis if historic team/player identities are reused publicly.
Codemasters' own historical catalogue can include third-party brands such as Micro Machines, which must be modeled as separate rights layers.
This batch suggests a Licensing Feasibility Score distinct from legal confidence: a title can have very clear rights yet be a poor licensing target because it is actively exploited.

architecture_finding.name: Licensing Feasibility Score
architecture_finding.reason: High-confidence ownership and high probability of obtaining a practical RGME license are different things.
